title: Budd and Keg Johnson as soloists
summary: The 1933 band had more sideman solos; Randolph praises Budd Johnson on tenor and Keg Johnson's lip-trilling trombone.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Now, the '33 band, there seemed to be more solos for the side men than in the earlier band. A lot of Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson solos.
Yes, that's right. Budd Johnson was a good tenor man, and Keg was a good -- those two Johnson boys, like, Budd (unintelligible), I mean, Keg is dead now.
Yes. Yes, he is. A fine (Unintelligible)
Yes, he was really -- I used to like to hear his -- he had a lip- trilling style, he went (musical sounds).
